meta.heroTitle: Hardware, CAD, wiring, code, and the revisions between them.
meta.heroIntro: I build projects where the mechanical design, electronics, software, and documentation all have to meet in the real world. This portfolio is organized around proof: what works, what changed, and what still needs to be improved.
meta.focusText: The goal is to show real build depth: hardware decisions, CAD constraints, wiring maps, test logs, project tradeoffs, and the exact revisions that made each design better.
meta.portfolioRuleText: Every major page should show evidence, not just claims.
meta.projectIndexText: These are the projects that best show the kind of engineering I care about: physical systems, real constraints, software that touches hardware, and enough documentation to make the design understandable.
meta.academicText: A small academic snapshot for context: the main portfolio is still project-first, but the coursework shows that the engineering work is backed by consistent school performance.
meta.smallerProjectsText: Not every useful project needs to be a flagship build. These smaller pieces show software practice, robotics experiments, visualization, and technical curiosity.
meta.skillSystemText: The point is not just that I know several tools. The important part is that the tools overlap: CAD affects wiring, wiring affects software, software affects testing, and testing decides the next design change.
meta.principlesText: The portfolio should read like an engineering notebook made presentable: specific, honest, and useful, with enough detail that another technical person can understand the work.
meta.recordTitle: A larger list of projects, school, competitions, Scouts, languages, and long-term learning.
meta.recordIntro: This page is intentionally broader than the main portfolio. It collects the work and experiences that give context to the engineering projects.
meta.contactText: Spring Early College Academy student and Exxon Teen Engineering + Tech Center participant focused on CAD, fabrication, electronics, robotics, embedded software, and technical documentation.
meta.projectVisualMapText: A quick visual map of the project's main subsystems and engineering evidence.

skillNarratives.title: Mechanical design
skillNarratives.text: I use CAD to reason through mechanisms before they become physical parts: clearances, assemblies, print orientation, mounting, and how the design will actually be built.

skillNarratives.title: Hardware + electronics
skillNarratives.text: My strongest projects combine wiring, sensors, actuators, power routing, and controller behavior instead of treating electronics as a separate afterthought.

skillNarratives.title: Software as a tool for hardware
skillNarratives.text: I write code to test, control, and explain real systems: MPF configs, hardware test utilities, embedded logic, web apps, and debugging workflows.

skillNarratives.title: AI-assisted engineering workflow
skillNarratives.text: I use ChatGPT as a reasoning partner for debugging, planning, documentation, and code review while keeping the design decisions grounded in real tests and constraints.

principles.title: Show the mechanism
principles.text: A good project page should make the working parts understandable: CAD, wiring, test setup, constraints, and the reason the design exists.

principles.title: Document revisions
principles.text: A failed wiring map, bad enclosure fit, or design mistake is valuable when it explains what changed and why the next version is better.

principles.title: Prefer working artifacts
principles.text: Finished polish matters, but the portfolio should prioritize real hardware, test videos, CAD screenshots, measurements, code, and build logs.
